subject: Qorex technical follow-up: request/response schema & streaming semantics
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@qorex.ai>
Cc: Devon Holt <devon.holt@qorex.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-28T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Qorex technical follow-up: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Hi Aisha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align the technical drop-in:

Meeting highlights:
- Primary goals: embed semantic search for knowledge base + a reranker stage to improve precision; enable tool-calling for live DB lookups; ship a reliable streaming UX for longer multi-turn support.
- Constraints you called out: hard limit on PII leaving the VPC, strict latency requirement for agent responses (~300–400ms p95 for short queries), and procurement wants clear SOW language on request/response schemas.

Open technical questions we promised to confirm:
1) SDK & auth: do you want API keys scoped per environment or mutual TLS inside your VPC? This affects onboarding flow and token rotation.
2) Routing & capacity: preference between cost-optimized (quantized models) vs. low-latency dedicated GPUs for production traffic?
3) Structured output / tool calling: you asked whether we can enforce JSON schemas from the model and return parseable events when a tool call is triggered.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: where will you host vectors (DB choice), and do you want Redwood to manage batching/refreshing embeddings?
5) Request/response schema specifics: chat vs completions, tokenization behavior for your mixed-language KB, max_tokens strategy, stop sequences for deterministic cutoffs, and streaming semantics for partial results.

Attachments: call recording + a proposed model operating plan (MOP).

Next steps I propose:
- Technical drop-in (45m) w/ Ben (runtime/SDK) and Karthik (integration) — can you share two 1-hour windows next week?
- In the drop-in we’ll walk a minimal integration: SDK auth flow, a sample tool-calling schema, and an embedding + reranker latency plan.

If helpful I can include a short decision matrix in advance showing tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs throughput) per routing option.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Attachments: qorex-20261028-recording.mp3 (audio), qorex-proposed-mop.pdf (PDF)

Date: 2026-10-29T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Qorex technical follow-up: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Thanks Vanessa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side before we lock in the drop-in:

Priorities to discuss in the technical call:
- We will host vectors in a managed vector DB (Pinecone) for now; ask: can Redwood pull-batch embeddings for reindexing and incremental refresh?
- Tool calling: yes, we need model outputs constrained to strict JSON payloads (inventory_lookup tool). What happens if the model produces malformed JSON? Do you provide deterministic schema validation and retries?
- Streaming: frontend team prefers server-sent events (SSE) style streaming with tokens arriving as they are generated. They also want an early partial 'embedding hint' so the UI can start local ranking while the model continues.

Questions on request/response specifics:
- Chat vs completions: for multi-turn agent flows, do you recommend the chat endpoint by default? What are the cost deltas we should expect for tokenization and context windows?
- max_tokens / stop behavior: we have several templated prompts where a strict stop sequence is important ("<END>") — does Redwood reliably honor stop sequences across streaming and quantized models?
- Tokenization: some of our KB is mixed Chinese/English — any gotchas in token counts and how that affects max_tokens?

I’m attaching a short requirements spreadsheet that lists desired guarantees and SLAs. Please confirm whether you can share a small integration checklist ahead of the call so our infra team can pre-provision the VPC peering and mTLS certs if needed.

Best,
Aisha Patel
Head of Product, Qorex
Attachments: qorex-requirements.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@qorex.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-30T11:17:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Qorex technical follow-up: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Hi Aisha — quick technical notes ahead of the drop-in (I'll bring reproducible examples):

1) SDK & auth:
- We support API keys (scoped, rotation-friendly) and mTLS for Private deployments. For VPC/private deployments, mTLS is the recommended route; tunneling to Hosted can be done but adds compliance checks.

2) Chat vs completions:
- Recommendation: use chat endpoint for multi-turn conversational agents and tool-calling. Chat maintains structured message history and has first-class tool-calling hooks (events for call, return, error).
- Completions are simpler for single-shot generation and may be slightly cheaper for short prompts, but you'll lose explicit tool-call lifecycle hooks.

3) Tokenization & max_tokens:
- Token counts vary by tokenizer; UTF-8 multi-byte chars (Chinese) typically compress to fewer tokens per character but you should instrument token counts during dev. We can share tokenization dev tools that estimate counts per prompt.
- Use max_tokens as a hard cap on generated tokens; for long context workflows we recommend prefixing with a truncation strategy (LRU or semantic) and using Redwood's SDK helper to compute remaining budget.

4) stop sequences & streaming semantics:
- stop sequences are supported across streaming. In streaming modes we emit an end-of-stream event when a stop sequence is detected; for quantized / lower-precision models we still apply sequence matching post-tokenization which is reliable for explicit delimiter tokens like "<END>".
- Edge case: if a model generates malformed JSON mid-stream, our SDK emits a partial event with the raw text plus a structured parse failure event. We can optionally auto-retry with a constrained steering prompt to attempt to re-output valid JSON.

5) Structured output / tool calling:
- Redwood supports tool-call events with typed JSON payloads; the control plane can validate against a provided JSON Schema and reject or request a re-generation. We also provide a schema-enforcement toggle: "reject-on-invalid" vs "attempt-repair".

6) Embeddings & rerankers:
- Typical pattern: 1) embed candidate docs, 2) retrieve top-K from vector DB (approx NN), 3) cross-encode top-K with a small reranker to produce final ranking. We can manage batching for embedding refreshes (incremental by doc id) and provide per-batch latency metrics. Our benchmark CSV attached shows median embed time on dedicated nodes.

Next steps:
- I’ll prepare a short demo repository showing: SDK auth (API key + mTLS stub), a chat flow with tool-calling + schema validation, and a streaming client (SSE).

Ben
Senior Engineer, Runtime
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Attachments: embedding-latency-benchmarks.csv

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@qorex.ai>

Cc: Devon Holt <devon.holt@qorex.ai>
Date: 2026-10-31T08:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Qorex technical follow-up: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before we book the drop-in:

- Canary / fallback: can you describe a canary rollout pattern if we start with hosted endpoints and then move to Dedicated GPUs? We need an automatic fallback if p95 latency exceeds threshold.
- Schema enforcement: we prefer "reject-on-invalid" for inventory_lookup for compliance. If you support an automatic repair path we’d like to see logs of attempted fixes.
- Truncation / continuation: if a response must be truncated due to max_tokens, can the SDK surface a continuation token or a clear flag so the UI can request a follow-up continuation?

If those are supported we can share two windows for the week of Nov 2 — Tue/Thu mornings (PST). Also, procurement wants a sample SOW line for the schema validation SLA (uptime and error-rate for schema rejections).

Appreciate it — Aisha

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@qorex.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Bcc: procurement@qorex.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Qorex technical follow-up: request/response schema & streaming semantics

Aisha — thanks, and great asks. Short answers and confirmed next steps: 

- Canary/fallback: yes — we support weighted routing across model variants and deployment tiers plus an automated fallback policy based on configured latency SLOs. We’ll draft a proposed canary plan showing traffic ramps and rollback criteria.
- Schema enforcement: we will default to "reject-on-invalid" for your inventory_lookup tool. When enabled, the SDK returns a 422-style parse rejection event and logs the raw output + token offsets to the integration logs. We can add a retention/archival SLA for those logs in the SOW.
- Truncation/continuation: the SDK surfaces a continuation cursor for truncated outputs and a boolean "truncated" flag in streaming and final responses. That cursor can be used to request a continuation call that preserves the conversation context but budgets the next chunk.

Action items (owners):
- Ben: prepare the demo repo + streaming SSE example (due 2026-11-05).
- Karthik: draft the canary rollout + SOW bullets for schema validation and log retention (due 2026-11-04).
- Vanessa: schedule the 45m technical drop-in for Tue Nov 3 9:30–10:15 PST (tentative) and circulate the integration checklist to your infra team.

We’ll also attach the sample SOW language and the MOP before the meeting. Looking forward to the drop-in — thanks for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
